mp.pillar: Sustained Dominance: higher positions, longer presence and higher peak positions on Most Popular.
observations: The top of Most Popular is led by Steal An Egg (75 days old) alongside multi-year evergreens like Brookhaven, Murder Mystery 2, 99 Nights in the Forest and RIVALS.
Movement was large below the top: Swing For Eggs (+24), Guess The Song (+19) and Sarab (+18) rose while Steal A Car, +1 Strength for Eggs and Search For The Needle each fell 24-29 places.
Seven games entered and seven left; new arrivals are mostly young (14-59 days) job sims, steal/egg titles and survival games, plus Dress Designer at 14 days.
By age, games past a year still hold the best median pillar percentile (62), while 4-12 month games sit at 36, which keeps the mid-life trough idea alive.
patterns: Higher-priced game passes (median above 149 Robux) tend to go with higher positions (H-mp-001, 63%), though established studios likely explain part of it.
All-caps titles tend to sit lower (H-mp-002, 64%), and titles asking for likes ('cta_like') also skew lower, which may mark low-effort clones.
Solo loops tend to hold lower positions than social ones (H-mp-003 strengthened to 59%); combat PvP and roleplay loops have the best median percentiles among profiled games.
A higher favorite rate per visit goes with lower positions, likely because huge evergreens accumulate visits far faster than favorites; this is a new hypothesis today.

outliers.name: Steal An Egg
outliers.note: A 75-day template game at the very top, against the evergreen pattern; template breakouts can briefly beat veterans.

outliers.name: RUNAWAYS [beta]
outliers.note: Popular, well-liked and well-monetized but fell 29 places, likely a gap between updates (last update 6 days ago).

takeaways.text: Holding a top spot may depend more on a lasting social loop (PvP or roleplay) than on a viral template; templates rise fast and fall fast.
Pass prices like an established game (most above 149 Robux) tend to go with higher positions, though studio maturity may explain much of it.
A template launch may fade between months 4 and 12 unless it adds a lasting hook.

te.pillar: Monetization Efficiency: earning a high position with modest CCU (Monetization Score ranks position × CCU, lower is better).
observations: The chart held 497 games with no entries or exits recorded today, so today's signal is about efficiency, not movement.
Donation and social-spending games again top efficiency (Donation Central, Summer Donations, Simple DONATIONS), along with prison and army roleplay and a party game.
The weakest efficiency comes from big-CCU games (Fish It!, Realistic Street Soccer) and young breakouts (Peel THE Potato, Makeup Mania at 13-17 days).
Games under 6 weeks old sit at the 19th efficiency percentile versus 57th past a year, the clearest lifecycle gap in the data.
patterns: Complexity strengthened today (rho +0.38 among 112 profiled games, H-te-013 now 67%): studio-scale games tend to earn more per player.
Pet/egg, '+1' and anime-themed games tend to earn a lower position for their CCU (all at 68%); 'Egg' (r -0.51) and 'Steal' (r -0.41) titles are the weakest keywords.
Live-ops signals (bracket tags, redeem codes, longer descriptions) consistently-ish go with better efficiency but are near the 70% threshold, not past it.
RPG and tower defense loops lead profiled efficiency; tower defense's median percentile is 91 but on only 2 games.

outliers.name: [CURE] Violence District
outliers.note: A large asymmetric horror game with high CCU and only cheap currency packs plus one VIP pass; it breaks the 'older is more efficient' rule, likely because its spending ladder is thin.

outliers.name: Fish It!
outliers.note: Huge CCU and 269 products but the weakest efficiency; sheer player count inflates the denominator.

takeaways.text: Depth tends to earn more per player: RPG progression, tower defense and competitive cosmetics beat template simulators on efficiency.
Price most developer products above 79 Robux and offer at least one premium item above 999 Robux; cheap impulse ladders alone may cap revenue per player.
Judge a new game's earning power after about day 43, not in its first month; monetization tends to lag popularity.
Treat efficiency extremes below about 1,000 CCU with caution because of the single daily CCU snapshot.

tt.pillar: Early Momentum: rapid upward movement on Top Trending, among games 0–4 months old only.
tt.metric: daily position gain on Top Trending
observations: Top Trending turned over heavily: 34 entries and 35 exits, the biggest churn so far.
Among games under 4 months, Lift Rock For Eggs (11 days, +52), Steal From The Rich! (+48) and Peel THE Potato (+35) gained most.
Many entries are old party or obby games resurfacing: Would You Rather Cartoons Tower (6+ years old, +52), Clone Engine (844 days), Mingle Carousel, Shrink Hide & Seek and Jump Clicker.
+1 Strength for Eggs fell 62 places and Steal A Car 36, so the '+1' and steal waves are cooling on this chart.
patterns: Party formats dominate today's entries: 1v1 table duels (Guess My Game, Spot and Paint, Hide In Pixels), would-you-rather towers and hide-and-seek variants.

Young games with a page video and verified creators climbed more slowly today (within-age effects -0.53 and -0.38), but q-values are high, so this may be noise or a sign that polished studio launches peak earlier.
Co-op loops may climb faster than solo or PvP ones (r +0.31), consistent with H-tt-008 (55%).
Upgrade-heavy and tycoon-money mechanics may slow momentum, echoing the '+1' slump.

outliers.name: Would You Rather: Cartoons Tower
outliers.note: A 2487-day-old game jumped +52, showing old party games can be re-surfaced, likely by recommendation shifts or creator video coverage.

outliers.name: Lift Rock For Eggs
outliers.note: A solo egg-hatching loop with the best momentum, a counter-example to the social-loop pattern.

takeaways.text: One clear hook stated briefly may help a new game place higher; shorter descriptions tend to go with higher positions.
Short-session party duels may be the current momentum format, but that is speculative after one day of entries.
Momentum may peak in weeks 3 to 6, so plan the first big update before about day 40.

uc.pillar: Breakout Popularity: higher positions within Up-and-Coming.
observations: Huss Valley (38 days), Get Your Driver's License! (9 days) and Peel THE Potato lead, with Sarab, Guess My Game and Firefighting Sim close behind.
16 games entered, including 2 Player Pizza Tycoon, Cut all the Grass!, Hide In Pixels, Makeup Frenzy (4 days old) and Rope an Animal.
Melt All The Ice (+33) and Film Animals (+24) rose; Swim For Eggs, Climb For Animals Eggs, Country Battles and Board Of Hell fell 24-37 places.
Games 14 days or younger hold a median percentile of 71 versus 49 for 15-42 days.
patterns: '+1' incremental games rank lowest (r -0.69, H-uc-003 now 61%), the strongest single effect on this chart.
Social play tends to beat solo loops among same-age games (H-uc-007 strengthened to 60%), with co-op the strongest social mode.
Character-art thumbnails may beat gameplay screenshots (within-age +0.35); added as a testable hypothesis today.
Recently updated games rank higher (rho -0.37 on days since update), also added for testing; reverse cause is possible since rising games update more.
Chore and real-life job framings (cut the grass, peel the potato, driver's license, firefighting) keep placing high, supporting H-uc-009 (57%).

outliers.name: Get Your Driver's License!
outliers.note: Second place with a 42% like ratio; the concept and novelty seem to matter more than reception early on.

outliers.name: Clone to Steal Eggs
outliers.note: A 97%-liked steal/egg game near the bottom, showing the steal template no longer guarantees a breakout.

takeaways.text: Avoid the '+1' incremental template for a breakout; it tends to rank lowest.
A social (especially co-op) loop tends to place higher than a solo one of the same age.
Mundane chores and real-life jobs may be an under-served niche for breakouts.
Character-art thumbnails may outperform gameplay screenshots; one day of data, so treat as speculative-to-may.

summary: The steal/egg template remains a popularity engine rather than a monetization engine: 'Egg' r=-0.51 and 'Steal' r=-0.41 on Top Earning efficiency while still filling Up-and-Coming, though several steal/egg games fell sharply today.
Complexity is the clearest cross-chart positive: +0.38 on Top Earning efficiency and +0.22 on Up-and-Coming.
Bracket tags still flip sign: helpful on Top Earning (+0.21), harmful on Top Trending (-0.26) and Up-and-Coming (-0.25), marking mature live-ops games rather than a breakout tool.
Page video goes with weaker momentum on both Top Trending (-0.41) and Up-and-Coming (-0.25); this may reflect studio launches that peak early, and needs more days.
Data is still thin: 3-4 days per chart, so most hypotheses sit between 50% and 68% and none has crossed 70%.
progressions: Real chart entries since tracking began: Top Trending 45, Up-and-Coming 26, Top Earning 22, Most Popular 13.

Entries by games already on another chart: Top Trending to Most Popular 10 (median 2 days), Up-and-Coming to Top Trending 9 (1 day), Top Earning to Top Trending 7 (2 days), Top Earning to Up-and-Coming 6 (3 days), Up-and-Coming to Top Earning 6 (1 day), Up-and-Coming to Most Popular 5 (1 day).
The Up-and-Coming to Top Trending to Most Popular path is the most common so far, but Top Earning is often reached early too, so the order is not strict.
